[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Gradient Descent Variants in Deep Learning: SGD, Momentum, and Nesterov"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Gradient descent is the backbone of optimization in deep learning. While standard Batch Gradient Descent computes the gradient of the entire dataset, it becomes computationally intractable for large datasets. To address this, variants such as Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD), SGD with Momentum, and Nesterov Accelerated Gradient (NAG) were developed to accelerate convergence and navigate complex loss landscapes."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Stochastic Gradient Descent updates the model parameters using the gradient computed from only a single training example (or a small mini-batch). This introduces high variance in the parameter updates, causing the loss function to fluctuate heavily, which can help the model escape local minima."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"# Standard SGD Parameter Update
weights = weights - learning_rate * gradient"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. SGD with Momentum"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"While SGD is efficient, it struggles in ravines where the surface curves steeply in one direction and gently in another, leading to oscillation. Momentum helps accelerate SGD in the relevant direction and dampens oscillations by adding a fraction (gamma) of the past update vector to the current update."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"V_t = gamma * V_{t-1} + learning_rate * gradient"},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"weights = weights - V_t"},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"# SGD with Momentum Implementation
velocity = gamma * velocity + learning_rate * gradient
weights = weights - velocity"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Nesterov Accelerated Gradient (NAG)"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Nesterov Accelerated Gradient is a slight variation of Momentum that provides a smart lookahead ability. Instead of calculating the gradient at the current position, NAG computes the gradient at the approximated future position (weights - gamma * V_{t-1}). This allows the algorithm to slow down before climbing up a slope, preventing it from overshooting."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Compute lookahead weights: weights_ahead = weights - gamma * velocity"},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Calculate gradient at lookahead: gradient = compute_gradient(weights_ahead)"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Update velocity and weights using the lookahead gradient."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"# Nesterov Accelerated Gradient Implementation
weights_ahead = weights - gamma * velocity
gradient = compute_gradient(weights_ahead)
velocity = gamma * velocity + learning_rate * gradient
weights = weights - velocity"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Choosing the right optimizer depends on the loss landscape geometry. Standard SGD is simple but slow in ravines. Momentum adds physical intuition to speed up training, and Nesterov provides a corrective mechanism to avoid overshooting, resulting in superior convergence properties for deep neural networks."}]
